To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we defined a multi-paradigm semantics to simulate SysML models using the SystemC-AMS language; (2) this semantics is based on the definition of a mapping from SysML to SystemC-AMS and the definition of a semantic adaptation for each language element; (3) we demonstrated the feasibility of our approach by implementing a tool that translates SysML models into SystemC-AMS, and by simulating a case study with the resulting code.

we have defined a concrete semantics for the most common elements of the SysML standard, we have added semantic adaptation rules to guarantee the correct interpretation of heterogeneous SysML models, and we have generated SystemC-AMS models from SysML diagrams.
we have developed a multi-paradigm formal semantics for SysML models and have used it to generate SystemC-AMS simulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the definition of semantics to enable a correct interpretation of heterogeneous systems models and to allow their simulation.
the formalization of the semantics of SysML, which is an important step toward the development of a SysML reference implementation.
the formal definition of semantics for the SysML standard and its use to enable the simulation of heterogeneous models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the work presented in this thesis contributes to the development of SysML by providing concrete semantics for its language elements and by adding semantic adaptation elements to ensure that interactions among different languages are unambiguous.
our work is the first attempt to provide a formal semantics for SysML and to use it to generate executable models.
our approach provides a way to automatically generate code for the simulation of SysML models, and that it allows for the validation of the system behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have defined semantics for SysML and we have used this definition to generate code in SystemC-AMS.
the proposed semantics and the translation approach allow the generation of executable models from SysML diagrams, enabling the simulation of the system behavior.
the proposed semantics is able to generate SystemC-AMS from SysML models, and the SystemC-AMS models are able to be simulated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of formal methods in the early stages of a project can reduce the risk of misunderstandings among different stakeholders and increase the confidence of the final product.
a formal semantics can be added to SysML to allow the automatic generation of SystemC-AMS models from SysML models, thus enabling the simulation of SysML models.
a precise definition of SysML semantics is a necessary step to guarantee interoperability and reusability of SysML diagrams.
